reviews.text: So far, the game has been quite enjoyable. I really like the different forms of skill expressions through the different ways the ship classes move combined with the Bullet Hell aspects. It gives you the ability to dodge attacks by baiting enemies/bosses into shooting into a specific direction and then moving in another. This sounds like something quite basic for most Action Rogue-Lite's but it's especially prominent in this game with the Ship-combat and much more restrictive movement compared to games like Hades, for example. In terms of bugs, most bugs I've encountered are issues with the controller and UI integration where you sometimes can correctly select an option with the controller properly but they aren't too bad. Other then that, I haven't encountered anything else. In general terms? I see a lot of potential for this game. It's just as fun and addicting as all the other good Action Roguelites around but separates itself quite good through the way the combat feels. Definitely worth the money and I hope I see a decent amount of updates from time to time

Most of the negative reviews I've seen begin with "I really wanted to like this game." Well, I really wanted to like this game. I have an "older system" at this point (g11 i7/3080) and it runs fine at 4k resolution (saw a few others with better systems having trouble, not my experience). So the game looks great and plays well, but that's not my problem. My problem is the game hates you, the player. I've played a LOT of the survival-style roguelight games (as most of my recent purchases can attest to) and I struggled with Starforged. First zone or two it seems reasonable: There are some badguy ships, you shoot them in their ship-faces and collect the loot. Sweet. Nice. Get some upgrades along the way of questionable help (one common upgrade I saw was going to boost my damage from 14.2 to 14.2. I guess it was a hundredth of a percent increase and wasn't even displayed). You start with 1 gun and can get up to 3 and it takes a while. Its mostly an auto-battler but you can take somewhat manual control over firing which seemed intermittently effective to me. You quickly learn that EVERY ship out there is faster than you are. They are able to move and reposition anywhere within the battlefield whenever they want to while you are limited by physics and reality. Eventually as you continue on through the map this means that enemy ships are clustered around you constantly, shooting at will and wearing you down. I was only ever to make any appreciable progress with the battleship in my 2 hours of play of the 3 starting ships but the last boss who had 127000 HPs and shields outlasted me. I'm doing between 40 and maybe 120 damage on a crit every few seconds. Its not enough. On top of that they LOVE their environmental hazards. There are zones that cover 90% of space, there are smaller areas that move through the map and others that appear out of nowhere and give you a bit of time to respond to and move, but they get layered ALL over the place. Your shield is pretty reliable, but I only found it to be effective on the battleship (the others were too low to do anything). Hull damage persists between nodes and is repairs are rare. TLDR: This game hates you. Its sad because its quite a pretty game. I don't need this kind of toxic relationship in my life. Refund requested.

EDIT: The devs already patched out a lot of my criticisms and complaints in my original review! Wow kudos to them! [b] [u] Definitely recommend [/u][/b] this now! [strike]Tentatively recommended now for $8.[/strike] There's actually a lot going for this game that asking $8 is bit of an undersell at this point. That said, I'd recommend waiting for some more tuning by the devs because the balance is pretty rough. Level up upgrades giving a tenth of a second faster reload time is.... oh ... oh so satisfying (not). You're only in each sector a limited amount of time before you're forced to jump, so any level up you get is very important as each sector becomes more challenging. That said, I'm sick of getting the majority of offered level up rewards being these 1/10th of a second reload speed buff or projectile speed buff. Really? The game will swarm you, as we'd expect in a survivors-like bullet-heaven, however it's to a point where it's unfair. You're slow, unless you get 10 of those 0.10 speed upgrades in a row, so you can't outrun the kamikaze ships or the million suicide ships with massive AOE. My CPU and GPU skyrocket to 100% utilization during initial startup and the shader compilation loading screen. I've seen this in other games where FPS isn't capped in the game during this process. But I'm not a dev. Loading between sector jumps can take longer than it should. I was concerned my PC crashed, but given the game isn't graphically demanding I was surprised this was the case. The sector loading time combined with the 100% utilization shader compilation at start up has me worried about how the game may crash or lag in hectic, late-game runs. All that aside, there's a lot of depth in the combat and meta progressions that I think it can be really fun after some balance passes. Right now, at least for me, it's too frustrating to keep trying the game out. I don't find joy in slamming my face against the wall for a couple hours to stack up meta upgrades to offset the poor level up cards you get during a run. I really like these space focused bullet heaven survivor games, so I look forward to coming back and seeing the progress the game has taken.

The developers have absolutely no idea how to handle balance and game design. When you first start, the game looks promising and visually appealing. However, after just two hours, you realize it isn't going anywhere. The first map of each run is incredibly basic and easy, featuring a tiny number of enemies that die in a single hit. That drastically changes on the very second map, which throws a massive wall of enemies at you that require multiple hits to bring down. To make matters worse, this isn't a true "bullet hell"—the enemies have guns, but they choose to blindly fly into you to ram your ship, dealing massive damage. Pretty suicidal chaps. The core issue is that even the fastest, most agile ship in the game is too slow and sluggish. The enemies fly faster and maneuver better than you can, even when your passive meta-progression skill tree is completely maxed out. Each ship starts with only one weapon, which is nowhere near enough to handle the barrage of enemies on screen. While other games in this genre give you active abilities to damage crowds and survive the onslaught, here you are entirely at the mercy of RNG. Additional weapons are tied to specific map rewards—if you get unlucky, you are forced to finish the entire run with just your single starting weapon. In similar titles like R.I.P., Jotunnslayer, or Greedland, leveling up grants you active skills that allow you to see the light at the end of the tunnel. Even when you fail a run, you know you are making tangible progress. Here? After three hours and a massive investment into the permanent upgrades, I still see no light. I have no idea how many dozens of times I am expected to grind these initial three maps before I am strong enough to defeat the first boss. This loop would be salvageable if the player ships weren't so incredibly sluggish, leaving you completely unable to evade the kamikaze swarms.

This game has some real potential, but also some real jank. Music is repetitive and droning, enemies are one note at best - basically just follow you around. Sound effects could also just genrally use a pass, plus eventually some kind of loose narative would be helpful for whyever we have to fight vice dread admiral peet or whatever. But the ship design is good, weapons are rather fun, and it fills a huge niche that was missing with the big chonky capital ship design. I want to FLY one of those, or even better BUILD one. Grab it on sale and hope the project keeps going. It'll need more investment, but there's something neat here.

Its a really fun game. However, it also gets to a point where FPS just got thrown out the window and the game crashes. I could play it for 20-30 minutes and then its just crash fest. I could play for hours on end. Its not even as graphics intensive as the other games that I play. But this really takes the cake on which games that could crash on me within the hour. -EDIT Okay now its not even funny how it just tanks so hard. I tried everything from lowering quality and resolution to window mode and all. I even tried going max graphics as it might be an issue with low graphics but sadly nothing worked. So unless they overhauled the FPS issue, I wont be playing this game anymore. -EDIT2 Dev Team fixed it and so far no more FPS drop. I haven't tested all the weapons yet but I think all got fixed. I hope theres also a tooltip for the ability during in-game just like the statuses as it would help to remind players what each ship does especially when trying new ships. Also, I hope theres a way to see what weapons your ship has when choosing maps as there are times I thought I had 5 weapons but instead had 6 and I chose a weapon node instead of a money or science. Lastly, I dont seem to find what a weapon's type is. I.e. a buff rewards you if you had more than one beam weapon and I thought had more than one but the buff did not indicate that I had only one so it was a wasted augment. Im sure players would get the hang of the game and these are just redundant things but these are just the things that I thought that could help in the learning curve when getting into the game in the first few hours. All the best!

took me 13h to be able to run the hardest difficulty and go for endless with only time beeing an issue. Basicly the game is fun but has a lot of rough edges. For Hord survival Rogu lite games it's NOT worth the money because you can be done in 10h if you have above average skills (aka more then mine ^^) . What you get is a very easy game to kill some time with what is sadly on the weaker side of the genre. The changes to the weapons are neglectable. The meta upgrades are as basic as it get's. The worst enemy i nthe game aren't the enemy ships or prijectiles or rocket or beam attacks... no the game is full of "Ground effects" that will ruin your day and I don't talk about ten at once or twenty I talk about screen vomit style everywhere stacked on each other. Oh and let's not forget forgett the endgame lag. Firing 6 laser weapons each shooting 150+ projectiles... LOL... isn't a healthy thing to do untill everything dies and you only kill respawns. Not to speak about pickung up everything on the map as soon as you spawn. You will get weaker by unlocking upgrades because you can't banish all the crap stuff you unlocked and like 80%+ of the unlocks are either niche or completely useless underpowered crap. So not unlocking stuff that isn't about firing faster, doing more dmg or crits ist making you weak so to speak. Sure in endless you don't care and pick up everything because why not... Still I'm far away to make something like a build and end up with a ton of crap I never wanted in my build. Yes I like the game it was fun to kill some time with and I would reccomend it to everyone who has some money left and time to kill. If you are on a budget or into very good games that offer something to write home about avoid this game like the plague or take another look at it in a few months. Hopefully the game will see some changes and become better. It's EA after all and I think the game might become better but for now it's not even mid.
